text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania has a huge crude oil refining capacity, President Emil Constantinescu told a Black Sea Economic Cooperation conference in Istanbul.
- A Black Sea Trade and Development Bank will open these days.
- World Bank President James Wolfensohn is expected to visit Romania on May 12.
- More than 50 percent of foreign investments in Romania come from European Union countries, statistics show.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania can act as an interface between Asia and Western Europe in trading, transport and refining Caspian crude, due to its infrastructure, Constantinescu said in Istanbul.
- Some 7,000 hectares of farmland were flooded in the western county of Arad due to late snows and heavy rainfalls.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Renel electricity authority threatens to cut power supplies to debtors who owe it a total 2.6 trillion lei.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Applications for Bucharest bourse listing from nine companies were approved. Another 70 companies have lodged their applications.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The head of the Romanian Intelligence Service will officially present his resignation on Wednesday before parliament gathered in a joint session of the two chambers.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel starts a two-day visit to Romania.
- Turkey will support Romania's bid to get early NATO admission, President Suleyman Demirel told his Romanian counterpart during a meeting in Ankara.
ADEVARUL
- Romania played its last card for NATO integration in Brussels, where Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea met ambassadors of NATO member countries, the newspaper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Ciorbea is confident Romania will join NATO in the first wave of the alliance's expansion, the newspaper says. ($=7,088 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
